name: AI token prices
question: Is AI getting cheaper to use?
metric: Median listed price per 1M tokens across AI models from their makers, with 3 input tokens per output token
solvedIf: Using AI becomes close to free
trendLabel: Median listed price in dollars per 1M tokens, per month, with 3 input tokens per output token.
rule: Getting cheaper when the median listed price is lower than a year before.

analysis.title: Are prices falling per model?
analysis.intro: Mostly not. The median falls because newer, cheaper models arrive, not because existing models get repriced.
points: Of 79 models listed both in 2025-11 and 2026-11, 71 kept their price, 4 got cheaper and 4 got more expensive.
Cheaper tokens do not always mean cheaper work, because a task can use more tokens on a newer model.
On the FrontierSWE benchmark, a hard task costs from about $99 of AI usage for a near-top score to about $1,030 for the top score.

Everyday use can cost far less. OpenCode reports an average of about 5 cents per session on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the most used model on its platform (OpenCode Data, opencode.ai/data, updated Nov 1, 2026, 10:18 AM UTC).

scoreReason: Down 88% since October 2023, when the data starts.

quote.author: Dax Raad
quote.text: with current token prices i wouldn't really say "cost of software is going to zero". our token cost is double our payroll which means even though we're 25 it's like we're 75. and i feel like our output is similar to a team of 75 pre-ai. we're just able to do it without all the downsides of a larger team. this is still a good thing. we couldn't hire 50 more people. so much overhead and impossible to retain a high bar
